predecessors.name: Republic of New Granada
predecessors.text: the Republic of New Granada, replaced by the Confederation when Congress approved the new Constitution on 22 May 1858

successors.name: United States of Colombia
successors.text: the whole Confederation, renamed the United States of Colombia by the Rionegro Constitution of 8 May 1863

ledger.x: 22 May 1858: Congress approves the Constitution that makes New Granada the Granadine Confederation.
8 May 1860: Mosquera takes Cauca out of the Confederation.
1861: Santander, Boyacá, Magdalena and Tolima stand with Mosquera.
18 July 1861: the rebels take Bogotá and the war's winning side takes the government.
8 May 1863: the Rionegro Constitution ends the Granadine Confederation.

wars.name: Colombian Civil War (1860–1862)
wars.outcome: Mosquera's rebels win: Bogotá falls on 18 July 1861, Mosquera becomes provisional president and the Conservative leaders die or give up by November 1862; the Rionegro Convention of 8 May 1863 creates the United States of Colombia.

certainty.note: The frontiers with Peru, Ecuador, Brazil, Venezuela and Costa Rica were claims and provisional treaties (the Ecuador line was set provisionally on 9 July 1856); the Amazon edge is soft throughout.
